content.intro: This lesson covers The Iterator Trait and Its Methods. It sits in Module 13, Closures and Iterator-Based Programming, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: The Iterator Trait and Its Methods matters when you work with reusable abstractions and type constraints. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Generics and traits let code express reusable behavior with compile-time type checking. Rust can use static dispatch for generic parameters or dynamic dispatch through trait objects.
